title: Distribution Rewards can be withheld or clawed back from an Integrator merely suspected or alleged to be non-compliant
content:
A.2.2.4.1.1.2 makes legal compliance a condition precedent to Distribution Rewards: Integrators "are solely responsible" for compliance, must "represent and warrant" it, and their "right to participate in the Integrator Program is contingent upon its ongoing compliance with all applicable laws and regulations."

A.2.2.4.1.1.2.1 then sets the enforcement standard remarkably low: "Sky Ecosystem Governance, in its absolute and unilateral discretion, retains the right to withhold, revoke, or **demand immediate repayment** of any and all Distribution Rewards from any Integrator that is **determined, suspected, or alleged** to be in violation of the Atlas or any legal, regulatory, or other obligations."

Three things stack here: suspicion or allegation suffices as a trigger, the discretion is absolute and unilateral, and the remedy reaches retrospectively to already-paid rewards. There is no adjudication step, no notice requirement, and no appeal route stated in this document.

The design logic is that Sky is exposed to regulatory risk through actors it does not control and cannot audit, so it buys the ability to sever and unwind fast rather than correctly. A.2.2.4.1.1.1 is consistent — alignment is judged by Operational GovOps and "Sky Core may choose whether to maintain an Integrator's Reward Code in its sole and absolute discretion."

The tension is with A.2.2.4.2: rewards are legally the Prime Agent's, but repayment can be demanded of the Integrator. A Prime Agent that has already passed through a negotiated share sits between an unwind demand and a counterparty with no contractual duty to return anything.
description: A.2.2.4.1.1.2.1 sets the trigger at "determined, suspected, or alleged" and grants absolute unilateral discretion, so no finding of actual violation is required.
